state.instructions: Assess the preservation claim from the supplied version semantics and current notification code.
state.facts: Paid/completed/reversed emission must preserve existing Booking.version checks used by correspondence and scheduled reminders. A separate trusted sales handler updating Booking.sale_phase would advance the parent version and stale those checks. Instead freeze original transaction source/amount/location/product/purchase time and four attribution values on Booking, while one unique CommercialSale child stores nullable phase and integer revision. The trusted check atomically finds or creates this child, changes only the child on phase transitions, then emits SaleMilestone using original monetary_due after allowance and Booking.source. DESIGN says child writes do not advance an unwritten parent. Positive original money plus paid payment, fulfilled reservation, consumed/not_required allowance, no cancellation/refund work and cumulative collected/refunded evidence admit paid; completed requires actual checked_out. Cancel/no_show/refund permanently reverses; review/expired invalidation reverses an existing published phase only, preserving pre-sale late-payment capacity recovery. Invoice independently validates ledger funds and complete customer history. ReservationChanged forwards to CommercialCheck; extra invalidation paths emit only CommercialCheck, so notices are not duplicated. Capture admission at original hour/day checkout checks verified identical actor/booker/capture account, same customer and latest_capture(customer,actor,location,product); quotes transport four validated frozen scalars and explicit product checked against resource.kind. Unattributed internal bookings remain valid. No cancellation_passed is emitted because refund cutoff does not prohibit cancellation. APIs and runner remain unimplemented.
state.actual_code:
A created row has version 1 throughout its creating transaction, including create-hook adjustments. Ordinary references to an existing row expose its admitted version `v` throughout the owner transaction while field reads observe ordered provisional changes. An accepted `set`, CRUD update or archive reserves `v+1`, even for a normalized same-value write. Further writes/calls/hooks to that row do not advance it again. Update-hook `event.before.version` is `v` and `event.after.version` is the reserved `v+1`; create-after is 1. Permanent removal has no after record; its deleted event carries `v+1`. A child write does not advance an unwritten parent. Failed operations advance nothing; receipt replay reapplies nothing. This write-intent rule intentionally produces history/version changes for accepted no-op writes. Locks compare stored values, not modification metadata.
